Replay

Shared turret

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Equip shared turret in an ability slot in staging. Q/E deploys it using the normal ability targeting. Walk within 64 units and press T to operate it; aim/fire with the mouse, and press T again to release it. Any living player can take a vacant turret. An occupied turret cannot be stolen.

The stock turret has 24 shared rounds, fires every six simulation ticks, and does two damage per ballistic shot. Switching operators preserves ammunition and the next-shot deadline. The final shot removes the turret and its occupancy in the same simulation tick. It never also fires the operator's handheld weapon in that tick; continuing to hold fire after dismount resumes normal weapon input.

Mounted players stay in place and cannot dash, cast, revive or fire their handheld weapon. Death, disconnect, player-generation replacement, teleport/warp and floor cleanup release them. Placement checks arena bounds, cover, line of sight and spacing; mounting checks range and line of sight. Invalid placement or a full eight-turret pool spends no cooldown. A full projectile pool spends no round.

Try dev/turret_workbench.tscn with F6, then Run isolated encounter. It equips and deploys the authored ability through normal game actions. The preview and encounter use the existing ability workbench. For a quiet shared test, launch the normal host/client with RSY_RUN=0 RSY_ENCOUNTER=turret, equip the ability, ready and start. Everyone needs the matching content-51/K build.

Responsibility Source
Inspector tuning data/deployables/shared_turret.tres, scripts/defs/turret_def.odin
Ability/cooldown data/abilities/turret.tres (ID 7)
Replayable lifetime, occupancy, ammo, firing shared/game/turret.odin
Detached view values shared/presentation/turrets.odin
Authored node composition entities/turret.tscn, scripts/views/turret.odin
Typed scene pool and targeted input scripts/turret_bridge.odin

The turret holds a generation-checked operator credit. There is no second mounted flag on Player, Godot ownership RPC, or timer to reconcile. Mount/release actions carry the turret's pool handle, so delayed input cannot operate a replacement turret that happens to occupy the same slot. Existing reliable action intents own queueing and outcome tracking; the reducer decides whether the claim succeeds. These actions use receipt timing alongside dash. Held aim/fire remain controls.

Rollback restores turret state with the rest of World. Correcting a predicted claim also corrects its shots and ammo. The scene pool follows that state through generation handles and scope changes. Seated clients use the predicted turret world; spectators use the delayed observed world, including its despawn timing. The scene handles barrel rotation, color and text; it has no gameplay authority.

Recovery carries occupancy, ammo and the next-shot deadline in the checkpoint. The real crash fixture kills the deployer's host process while a surviving player is operating the turret, checks the restored operator/ammo, then hands it to a third player and empties it. If the departed host was the operator, ordinary disconnect cleanup releases the turret instead.

Content advances from 50/J to 51/K (0x525343524150304b), protocol 7 unchanged. The offline converter accepts content 50 as well as prior supported revisions. Frozen old catalog/action contracts map explicitly to the new shape; old runs receive an empty turret pool and zero turret definitions/targets. Conversion preserves their original catalog rather than adding this ability to an existing run. The historical recording verifier accepts --content50. See saves.

The authoring exercise fit the existing framework without adding transport, rollback, recovery or code-generation primitives. The main extra work was schema evolution: adding a targeted action and a new ability family required freezing the old action type and explicitly mapping the extended enum. Gameplay remains a small value-state feature plus a scene adapter; compatibility code is separate.

Run the focused suite from the repository root:

Shell
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_turret/run.sh

It covers contention, handoff, exhaustion, forced dismount, stale handles, placement/cover/capacity, late correction, occupied checkpoint continuation, content-50 import, native/WASM equality, the authored workbench, three real peers and occupied host-crash recovery. Browser compilation and pure WASM execution are covered; this feature has not had a separate interactive browser or human balance playtest. See the implementation receipt.
